release.name: Touchless v0.2.623
release.notes:
# v0.2.623

- **A switch no longer moves its row (#1031).** In Automations, turning an automation on or off made its card jump to
  another place in the list while your finger was still over it, so the next tap could land on another automation's
  switch.
  - Now a card stays where it is while the list is on screen. The list is put in order again the next time you open
    it, when you come back to the app, or when you pick another order.
  - The same goes for Scripts, Triggers, Webhooks, Event Hub watches, Learned skills, App skills and the ready-made
    rules in AI instructions.
- **"Active first" is your choice (#1031).** The sort menu of Automations now ends with "Active first", and the sort
  button says so: "Active · Newest first".
  - On (as before): the automations that are on come first, then the ones turned off.
  - Off: only the order you picked counts. The finished ones stay under "Inactive".
  - An AI can read or change it with the `automations_active_first` setting.

release.name: Wallify 0.8.0
release.notes:
- **Smart wallpapers** - a third side of the switch at the top of Home: *Live · Photos · Smart*. A smart wallpaper is
  drawn on the phone from its real time and state: a clock that tells the time, a tank as full as the battery, the
  sky as it is now. What you browse is the wallpaper itself, running on your phone.
- **24 of them**, in five groups. *Clocks*: Cockpit, Word Clock (the time in words, in Hebrew too), Orbit, Neon,
  Synthwave, Time Rings, Classic, Big Time, This Month, Year in Dots. *Sky & weather*: Weather Now (the real sky with
  drifting clouds, rain, snow, lightning, fog), Forecast, Sky Now, Daylight (the sun's path, sunrise and sunset),
  Aurora, Tonight's Moon. *Calendar*: My Day, Next Up, Day Planner. *Places*: Earth Now (a world map lit where it is
  day), Compass, World Time. *Device*: Liquid Battery (leans with the phone, bubbles while charging), Device HUD.
- **Make it yours** - *Customize* gives each wallpaper the options that fit it: colours, switches, a city from a list
  of the world's cities (the three cities of World Time; the place a weather or sky wallpaper is for), Celsius or
  Fahrenheit, the Word Clock's language, your own words on the Classic dial. Every change is drawn at once.
- **Your calendar on the wallpaper** - choose which calendars are shown. Wallify asks to read the calendar only when
  you pick calendars for such a wallpaper; the meetings are only read on the phone and drawn, never sent anywhere.
  On a locked phone a meeting keeps its time but shows *Busy* instead of its name and place (a switch turns that
  off).
- **Weather without a location permission** - the weather comes from Wallify Cloud, which finds the city from the
  phone's network address; it is asked for only while such a wallpaper is on screen, at most every half hour.
  Offline, these wallpapers show the time and say so.
- **Love it, like any wallpaper** - the heart, a double tap or touch and hold; setting one loves it too. Loved smart
  wallpapers have their own *Smart* tab in Favorites. The Smart feed is in a new order on every visit.
- **Easy on the battery** - a smart wallpaper is drawn only while it is on screen: once a minute, once a second, or
  in frames only for what really moves (a second hand, rain); hidden, it does nothing.
- Set one with *Set*: the first time Android's own "Set wallpaper" screen opens for *Wallify Smart* (home, lock or
  both); after that a change shows at once. Wallify Smart is a wallpaper of its own beside Wallify Live, so moving
  between a video and a smart wallpaper goes through that screen.
- Not yet: sharing, comments and love counts for smart wallpapers, and their place in the favourites wallpaper that
  takes turns - they are not in Wallify Cloud's catalogue yet.

release.name: Touchless Bridge 1.1.22
release.notes:
**Installing over 1.1.21 or older: remove the old app first, once.** This version is signed with a new key, so
Android won't install it on top of an older copy ("App not installed"). Uninstall Touchless Bridge, install
1.1.22, then connect the phone and sign in to HackerAI again. Later versions update in place as before.

A new look, an easier start, a new icon, and the app now shows when HackerAI is working.

- **You can see HackerAI working.** While HackerAI works in the chat, the app's icon in the status bar moves, and
  the notification says "HackerAI is working" with the step it is on right now ("Thinking...", "Opening Maps",
  "Phone tool: get battery status", "Running a command: nmap") and a running clock. Opened, it lists the last few
  steps. Home shows the same line. It keeps following after you close the chat window, and goes quiet when
  HackerAI is done. Only a short line per step is shown, never a command's arguments or its output.
- **The chat stays where you left it.** Closing the chat window no longer throws the page away: open it again and
  it is there at once, also in the middle of a task. A chat left idle for 10 minutes is let go and loads fresh.
- **`touchless … --say "…"` and `--done` work on the phone too** (when the phone itself is the HackerAI machine),
  as they do on a computer. The setup prompt now shows the real form: `touchless call <tool> key=value`.
- **New icon.** A hooded figure whose face is a terminal prompt (`>_`). It also has a themed-icon version, and the
  "Running" notification uses it.
- **Home shows where you stand.** A status card with the phone, Touchless and HackerAI as three points on a line.
  When the phone is connected a glowing packet travels from it to Touchless, and on to HackerAI once you're signed
  in there; while the phone isn't connected nothing moves. A button takes you to HackerAI.
- **The animation shows on every phone**, also where the phone's own animations are turned off. Settings › about ›
  "Animate the status" turns it off.
- **One thing to do on Home: connect your phone.** With a Paste button, and "Open Touchless", which opens the
  Touchless app to copy your address. Once the phone is connected the card folds away and HackerAI opens by itself.
- **HackerAI in the middle of the bottom bar.** One tap from anywhere.
- **Settings in cards.** Connection, HackerAI, always on, about. A line that isn't connected takes you back to
  Home. Running the bridge on the phone itself is now one switch in the connection list, "Remote Control on this
  phone". The setup prompt can be sent again, not only copied.
- **"Check for updates" answers.** It says "No newer version found" when there is nothing newer.
- **Battery.** Settings shows when battery use is already unrestricted, and the button only when it isn't.
- **The chat shows a page loading** with a thin line along the top.
- **Back from Settings** returns to Home.

release.name: Israel App Manager 1.0.3
release.notes:
- **Always the newest version.** The app no longer waits for its catalog to notice a release: every time the list is loaded it asks each app's releases page on GitHub itself, and offers a release the moment it is out.
- **Install and Update check once more** at the moment you tap them, so what gets installed is the newest release, never one that needs another update right after.
- Coming back to the app after a few minutes refreshes the list on its own; pulling down always does.
- Update notifications and the app's own update use the same check.
